docs.title: TERRA Data Ingestion Module
docs.text:
The Data Ingestion Module is a Python 3.12+ FastAPI service that exposes registered Sentinel-2 ingestion processes through a validated HTTP API.

It integrates two independently maintained components:

  • UC1 — forecaster-collector: Runs the TERRA UC1 Sentinel-2 collector, installed from a pinned Git revision.
  • UC3 — coastal-uc3-sentinel2: Runs the TERRA UC3 ingestion package, supplied as a private Python wheel.

Both profiles use the same API and execution infrastructure while keeping their collector implementations, configuration, and storage responsibilities separate.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Validate common and profile-specific requests with Pydantic.
  • Dispatch requests only to registered profiles.
  • Run synchronous collectors in worker threads.
  • Prevent concurrent runs for the same AOI within one API process.
  • Connect to CDSE, MongoDB, and MinIO through the selected collector.
  • Return orchestration metadata and structured collector results.
  • Report independent readiness for UC1 and UC3.

docs.title: Supported profiles
docs.text:
Profile Workflow forecaster-collector Restore UC1 collection state, discover and collect observations, and publish statistical data and artifacts. coastal-uc3-sentinel2 Discover Sentinel-2 L2A scenes, assess acquisition quality, retrieve raster imagery, and publish scene metadata and artifacts.

Requests are synchronous: the API responds after the selected profile finishes. The service does not provide a background job queue or a persisted API-level job model.

docs.title: External dependencies
docs.text: The UC1 collector is installed from its pinned Git revision. The UC3 package is privately distributed and is not included in this repository; supply it through an authorized handoff or private artifact channel. Access, use, modification, and redistribution remain subject to the respective maintainers' permissions and licensing terms.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The module exposes a synchronous REST API for two Sentinel-2 workflows. Both use provider: "sentinel-2"; profile selects the adapter and determines which request fields and persistence operations apply.

Profile Workflow forecaster-collector UC1 statistical collection and processing coastal-uc3-sentinel2 UC3 Sentinel-2 L2A scene selection, quality checks, raster delivery, and publication

docs.title: Base URLs
docs.text:
Local development: http://127.0.0.1:8000

Production: https://server.iprism.eu/data-ingestion

Append endpoint paths to the base URL. In production the reverse proxy serves the application under /data-ingestion. Interactive OpenAPI documentation is at /docs (under the production prefix, /data-ingestion/docs).

docs.title: GET /health/live
docs.text:
Reports that the API process is running. It does not contact external dependencies.

{"status":"ok"}

HTTP status: 200.

docs.title: GET /health/ready
docs.text:
UC1 readiness check. It loads UC1 storage/provider configuration, pings the configured MongoDB database, and calls MinIO head_bucket for the UC1 bucket. It does not write data or contact the satellite provider. A configuration failure marks MongoDB and MinIO skipped; failed connectivity marks the affected dependency unavailable.

{
  "status": "ready",
  "checks": {"configuration":"ok", "mongodb":"ok", "minio":"ok"}
}

HTTP status is 200 when ready and 503 otherwise. The body has the same shape when not ready, with status: "not_ready" and per-check states.

docs.title: GET /health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2
docs.text:
UC3 readiness is checked independently. It imports the installed UC3 package and loads its acquisition schema, validates UC3 storage/provider settings and the authorised AOI registry, pings MongoDB, then lists at most one object under the configured UC3 scene-input prefix. If package/configuration checks fail, later dependency checks are skipped.

{
  "status": "ready",
  "checks": {"package":"ok", "configuration":"ok", "mongodb":"ok", "minio":"ok"}
}

HTTP status is 200 when every check is ok, otherwise 503. This does not test CDSE authentication, execute a catalogue/process request, or prove MinIO write permission. UC3 readiness does not change UC1 readiness.

docs.title: POST /api/ingestion/run
docs.text: Runs the selected profile in a worker thread and keeps the HTTP request open until it finishes. A normal collector outcome (including UC3 no_data or failed) is returned with HTTP 200; HTTP errors are reserved for validation, configuration, availability, concurrency, and unexpected execution errors described below. There is no job queue, 202 Accepted, or polling endpoint.

docs.title: Common request fields
docs.text:
Field Required Contract run_job_id Yes Non-empty orchestration/correlation identifier. UC3 also uses it as the package correlation ID. triggered_at Yes ISO 8601 datetime with a timezone offset. provider Yes Literal sentinel-2. profile Yes forecaster-collector or coastal-uc3-sentinel2. aoi_id Yes Non-empty AOI identifier. UC3 additionally checks it against the configured authorised AOI registry. bbox Yes Four WGS84 numbers [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat]; must be ordered and within longitude/latitude ranges. UC3 also checks it matches the registered AOI.

The outer request model permits extra fields by Pydantic's default behavior. The nested uc3 object explicitly rejects unknown fields. UC1-only fields are not forwarded to the UC3 package.

docs.title: UC1: forecaster-collector
docs.text:
run_name is required for UC1. Other optional UC1 fields are:

Field Default / constraints history_start 2016-01-01 target_date Current UTC date when omitted mode auto; allowed: auto, backfill, incremental max_days_per_run Optional positive integer max_tiles_per_run Optional positive integer

Example:

{
  "run_job_id": "job-sperchios-001",
  "triggered_at": "2026-08-14T07:30:00+03:00",
  "provider": "sentinel-2",
  "profile": "forecaster-collector",
  "aoi_id": "sperchios",
  "bbox": [22.433493, 38.837552, 22.569555, 38.894223],
  "run_name": "sperchios",
  "history_start": "2016-01-01",
  "target_date": "2026-08-14",
  "mode": "auto",
  "max_days_per_run": 1,
  "max_tiles_per_run": 1
}

Execution calls the installed data_collection collector with publication enabled. It discovers and collects the missing Sentinel-2 tile/date observations, processes them, and maintains local run/history/state outputs. For persistence it reads existing AOI observations and checkpoints from MongoDB, uploads/updates artifacts and metadata in MinIO/MongoDB, and writes its pipeline-run state. Exact provider calls and number of DB/object operations depend on the requested date range, missing observations, and persisted state; this is not a single fixed database query.

UC1 result fields are those returned by the installed collector's CollectionResult.to_dict(). Common outcomes are success, partial, and failed.

docs.title: UC3: coastal-uc3-sentinel2
docs.text:
UC3 requires the nested uc3 options. Storage credentials, provider credentials, database names, bucket, and prefixes come from worker environment configuration (UC3_INGEST_*); they are not accepted as request options.

uc3 field Required Contract contract_version Yes Literal integer 2. mode Yes latest or window. time_from, time_to Yes Timezone-aware datetimes; time_to must be later. selection_policy No uc3_parity_pilot by default; alternatively uc3_monthly_backfill. max_scenes No Strict integer 1–24; omitted value/policy defaults are resolved by the package. project_id No Optional request value; the package scopes execution to its configured project. request_id No Optional package request identifier. registry_version No Optional AOI registry version. window_id No Optional acquisition window identifier.

Example:

{
  "run_job_id": "uc3-aoi01-20261008-001",
  "triggered_at": "2026-10-08T00:05:00Z",
  "provider": "sentinel-2",
  "profile": "coastal-uc3-sentinel2",
  "aoi_id": "aoi_01",
  "bbox": [-2.88294, 56.33412, -2.80112, 56.3715],
  "uc3": {
    "contract_version": 2,
    "mode": "latest",
    "time_from": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z",
    "time_to": "2026-10-08T00:00:00Z",
    "selection_policy": "uc3_parity_pilot",
    "max_scenes": 1
  }
}

The adapter passes run_job_id, trigger time, provider/profile, AOI, bbox, and uc3 options to the package after checking the AOI registry. The package then builds and validates its acquisition request, searches the CDSE catalogue for Sentinel-2 L2A candidates, applies its tile/AOI quality selection, and requests five-band reflectance rasters from the CDSE Process API for selected scenes. The package publishes accepted rasters to the configured MinIO namespace and commits scene, scene-asset, and artifact metadata in MongoDB. It checks committed artifacts to support reuse/idempotency. If no candidates pass selection, it returns no_data and does not publish a scene package. The exact catalogue pages, process calls, and MongoDB/MinIO operations depend on matches, quality results, and existing committed assets.

docs.title: Response structure
docs.text:
The API wraps each adapter result in this application-owned envelope. status is copied from collector_result.status (or unknown if a collector omits it); timestamps and duration are measured by the API. UC1 and UC3 collector payloads have different contracts.

{
  "run_job_id": "job-id",
  "provider": "sentinel-2",
  "profile": "forecaster-collector",
  "aoi_id": "sperchios",
  "triggered_at": "2026-08-14T07:30:00+03:00",
  "started_at": "2026-08-14T04:30:01Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-08-14T04:30:04Z",
  "duration_ms": 3000,
  "status": "success",
  "collector_result": {"status":"success"}
}

collector_result is abbreviated above. The real payload is the selected collector's dictionary and is not normalized into a shared inner schema.

docs.title: UC1 response
docs.text: The UC1 payload is CollectionResult.to_dict(). For example, a no-new-data run may return status: "success", empty date lists, zero new records, and paths to its persisted history/state outputs. A run can also return partial or failed. Paths such as outputs/sperchios/... are worker-local paths, not necessarily downloadable API URLs.

docs.title: UC3 response
docs.text:
The UC3 payload is the package's wp2_run_response result. The following is a consistent excerpt from the installed package's no-data fixture; all three status/outcome fields agree and there are no scene assets because no scene was delivered:

  "provider": "sentinel-2",
  "profile": "coastal-uc3-sentinel2",
  "aoi_id": "aoi_01",
  "triggered_at": "2026-10-08T00:05:00Z",
  "started_at": "2026-10-08T00:05:00Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-10-08T00:05:00Z",
  "duration_ms": 0,
  "status": "no_data",
  "collector_result": {
    "schema_version": 2,
    "result_type": "uc3_ingestion_result",
    "package_version": "0.5.1",
    "profile": "coastal-uc3-sentinel2",
    "request_id": "uc3req_0f610d29f7c25189afd117bb7fc9652e",
    "correlation_id": "example-airflow-run",
    "aoi_id": "aoi_01",
    "mode": "latest",
    "publish": true,
    "outcome": "no_data",
    "reason": "no_scene_passed_aoi_quality",
    "error": null,
    "started_at": "2026-10-08T00:05:00Z",
    "completed_at": "2026-10-08T00:05:00Z",
    "output_grid": {"crs":"EPSG:4326", "width":505, "height":414, "approx_pixel_size_m":[9.993,9.981]},
    "selection": {"catalogue_entries":1, "acquisitions":1, "passed_tile_prefilter":1, "considered":1, "aoi_quality_policy":"uc3_aoi_scl_unusable_v1", "max_scenes":3, "delivered":0},
    "candidates": [
      {
        "provider":"CDSE",
        "provider_scene_id":"S2B_MSIL2A_20260824T113319_N0512_R080_T30VWH_FIXTURE.SAFE",
        "acquisition_key":"S2B_20260824T113319",
        "duplicate_tile_scene_ids":[],
        "collection":"sentinel-2-l2a",
        "processing_level":"L2A",
        "acquired_at":"2026-08-24T11:35:31.331Z",
        "cloud_cover_pct":12.0,
        "platform":"sentinel-2b",
        "constellation":"sentinel-2",
        "decision":"rejected_aoi_quality",
        "aoi_quality":{"policy_id":"uc3_aoi_scl_unusable_v1", "max_aoi_unusable_pct":10.0, "probe_resolution_m":60.0, "aoi_unusable_pct":62.0, "aoi_cloud_pct":62.0, "aoi_cloud_shadow_pct":0.0, "aoi_nodata_pct":0.0, "aoi_other_unusable_pct":0.0, "status":"rejected"}
      }

    "scene_packages": [],
    "status": "no_data",
    "scene_asset_ids": []

}

For completed, accepted candidates have corresponding entries in scene_packages; scene_asset_ids is derived from those packages. Each scene package contains identifiers, scene/quality/raster/processing metadata, a committed artifact delivery reference (bucket/object key/hash), and provenance. For failed, the package returns outcome/status: "failed" and may include a structured error object. The API copies the package result and mirrors its status in the outer response. UC3 outcomes completed, no_data, and failed all normally use HTTP 200.

Clients should inspect the outer status and, for UC3, collector_result.outcome, collector_result.reason, and collector_result.error; do not treat HTTP 200 alone as a successful acquisition.

docs.title: Request validation (422)
docs.text:
FastAPI/Pydantic rejects malformed request bodies before the adapter runs. This includes unknown profile/provider, invalid bbox order/range, missing profile-required fields, invalid UC3 times/options, and extra keys inside uc3. FastAPI uses its standard validation body, for example:

{"detail":[{"loc":["body","uc3","mode"],"msg":"Input should be 'latest' or 'window'","type":"literal_error"}]}

docs.title: Handled adapter errors
docs.text:
The application returns {"detail":{"code":"...","message":"...","run_job_id":"..."}} for mapped execution errors.

HTTP Code Typical cause 400 collector_configuration_error Invalid/missing adapter configuration, or UC3 AOI/bbox not authorised. 409 collector_already_running Another request for the same guarded AOI is running in this process. 503 collector_unavailable UC3 package/runtime cannot be imported or another explicitly unavailable dependency is detected. 500 collector_execution_error Unexpected collector error or invalid/inconsistent UC3 result.

UC1 storage preflight errors are mapped to 400 (configuration) or 503 (connection). UC3 configuration errors raised by the package are mapped to 400; provider or storage failures represented as a valid UC3 result may instead produce HTTP 200 with status: "failed". Unhandled failures outside the adapter's mapped exceptions use FastAPI's normal server-error handling.

Messages are sanitized for adapter execution failures. Validation messages may contain the invalid field/value supplied by the caller; never put credentials in request fields.

docs.title: Execution and deployment notes
docs.text:
• Calls are synchronous and can take as long as catalogue discovery, raster processing, and publication. Set client and reverse-proxy timeouts accordingly.
  • The AOI concurrency guard is process-local; it does not coordinate multiple API replicas.
  • Readiness reports connectivity/configuration checks and does not guarantee CDSE authentication, a matching scene, or successful writes.
  • UC3 API responses include storage object keys and artifact metadata, not raster bytes or a download endpoint.
  • The UC3 package must be installed in the runtime image and its server-side UC3_INGEST_* settings must be configured.

See UC3 Integration Documentation for package installation, environment setup, and manual execution guidance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Data Ingestion Module is a FastAPI-based service that provides a unified interface for executing different data ingestion workflows.

The architecture follows a profile-based execution model, separating HTTP request handling, validation, profile selection, collector integration, and data persistence.

Each ingestion profile encapsulates a specific collection workflow while sharing the application's API and execution infrastructure.

Currently supported profiles:

  • forecaster-collector (UC1): Sentinel satellite data collection and statistical processing for forecasting applications.
  • coastal-uc3-sentinel2 (UC3): Sentinel-2 scene acquisition, quality assessment, raster processing, and publication.

New ingestion workflows can be introduced by implementing an adapter and registering the corresponding profile, without modifying the core API architecture.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
The application separates common infrastructure from profile-specific functionality.

Layer Location Responsibility FastAPI application app/main.py Initialise the application and register API routers. HTTP routes app/api/routes/ Handle requests, translate errors into HTTP responses, and construct response envelopes. Request/response schemas app/schemas/ Validate common and profile-specific inputs and define API contracts. Profile service app/services/ingestion.py Resolve registered profiles and coordinate execution. Profile adapters app/adapters/ Translate API requests into collector-specific contracts, manage execution boundaries, and normalise errors. External collector packages Installed dependencies Implement acquisition, processing, and persistence operations. Configuration Environment-based settings Provide profile-specific credentials, storage connections, and runtime parameters. Storage infrastructure MongoDB and MinIO Persist collection metadata, processing state, and generated artifacts.

The FastAPI application remains independent of the internal implementation details of individual collectors.

docs.title: Request Dispatch
docs.text:
All supported ingestion profiles are accessed through a common endpoint:

POST /api/ingestion/run

                    HTTP Client
                         |
                         v
                  FastAPI Endpoint
                         |
                         v
                  Request Validation
                         |
                         v
                   Profile Registry
                         |
             +-----------+-----------+
             |                       |
             v                       v
        UC1 Adapter              UC3 Adapter
             |                       |
             v                       v
       UC1 Collector             UC3 Package
             |                       |
             +-----------+-----------+
                         |
                         v
              Profile-Specific Result
                         |
                         v
                API Response Envelope

The profile registry maps a predefined profile identifier to its corresponding adapter.

forecaster-collector   -> UC1 collector adapter
coastal-uc3-sentinel2  -> UC3 ingestion adapter

Profiles are controlled extension points. API callers may select only registered profiles and cannot specify arbitrary modules, functions, or executable commands.

Because collector operations are potentially blocking, adapters execute through the application's worker-thread infrastructure.

The HTTP request remains open until execution completes.

docs.title: Adapter and Collector Integration
docs.text:
Each adapter provides a consistent boundary between the ingestion API and its underlying collection implementation.

Adapters are responsible for:

  • Translating validated API requests into collector-specific input contracts.
  • Invoking the corresponding collector or external Python package.
  • Managing process-local concurrency restrictions.
  • Translating known exceptions into application-level errors.
  • Returning structured results compatible with the shared API response envelope.

The collectors retain responsibility for their domain-specific operations, including data discovery, acquisition, processing, validation, and publication.

This design allows collectors to evolve independently without requiring changes to the common HTTP interface.

docs.title: Persistence Boundary
docs.text:
The ingestion API does not directly manage collector data persistence.

Each collector owns its storage operations and interacts with the infrastructure according to its own data model.

                  FastAPI Application
                          |
                    Profile Adapter
                          |
                          v
                  Collector Package
                          |
              +-----------+-----------+
              |           |           |
              v           v           v
         External API   MongoDB     MinIO
              |
         Data Acquisition
              |
         Processing / Validation
              |
         Result Publication

The main persistence responsibilities are:

  • MongoDB: Stores queryable collection metadata, observations, scene information, processing state, and execution records, depending on the profile.
  • MinIO: Stores raster files, JSON/GeoJSON artifacts, collection outputs, manifests, and other binary or structured artifacts.
  • Local storage: Provides temporary execution and processing space where required by the collector.

Storage namespaces, collection structures, and persistence strategies remain profile-specific.

Local filesystem artifacts are not assumed to be persistent or accessible across container instances.

docs.title: Configuration and Dependency Isolation
docs.text:
Each ingestion profile maintains its own runtime configuration and credentials.

Configuration is supplied through environment variables and validated by the corresponding collector or adapter.

For example:

  • UC1 uses its existing collection and storage configuration.
  • UC3 uses the dedicated UC3_INGEST_* configuration namespace.

Although profiles may share infrastructure such as MongoDB, MinIO, or external data providers, their configuration and data namespaces remain logically separated.

External collector packages are installed as application dependencies. The UC3 integration uses a privately distributed Python wheel, whereas the UC1 collector uses its established dependency mechanism.

docs.title: State and Restart Behavior
docs.text:
State management is delegated to individual collectors.

Depending on the profile, collectors may support:

  • Restoration of previously collected data.
  • Incremental acquisition based on stored processing state.
  • Reuse of previously published artifacts.
  • Skipping already completed collection units.
  • Recovery from interrupted or partially completed operations.

The application does not impose a common persistence or recovery algorithm on all profiles.

Container restarts do not automatically imply a complete re-acquisition. Actual recovery behavior depends on each collector's implementation and the availability of its persisted state.

docs.title: Health and Readiness
docs.text:
The service provides common liveness checks and independent readiness checks for supported ingestion profiles.

Endpoint Purpose GET /health/live Application liveness GET /health/ready UC1 configuration and storage readiness GET /health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2 UC3 package, configuration, and storage readiness

Profile-specific readiness checks validate the dependencies required for that profile without triggering collection operations.

A failure in one profile's readiness does not necessarily indicate that other profiles are unavailable.

docs.title: Current Operational Limits
docs.text:
• Ingestion requests are synchronous from the HTTP client's perspective and remain subject to client, reverse-proxy, and server timeouts.
  • Collector execution occurs in worker threads to avoid blocking the FastAPI event loop.
  • Concurrent execution guards operate within individual application processes.
  • Multiple application replicas do not share a distributed execution lock.
  • The deployment expects required external services, including MongoDB and MinIO, to be accessible through the configured infrastructure.
  • There is currently no centralised background job queue or persistent job polling mechanism.
  • The application does not introduce its own dedicated authentication and authorisation mechanism for ingestion requests; access control must be enforced at the deployment boundary.

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
The architecture is designed to accommodate additional ingestion profiles without restructuring the application.

Integrating a new collector generally involves:

  1. Defining its request validation requirements.
  2. Implementing an adapter for the collector's execution contract.
  3. Registering the profile in the application dispatcher.
  4. Configuring its dependencies and storage access.
  5. Adding profile-specific readiness checks and integration tests.

This maintains a consistent API while allowing different ingestion implementations, data providers, processing pipelines, and storage models to coexist within the same service.

docs.title: Transitioning Team Collection Logic into Independent Collector Packages
Purpose
docs.text:
This guide explains how a collaborating team should move its existing data-collection requests and processing code into an independently installable collector package that is invoked by the Data Ingestion Module.

The intended end state is that the Data Ingestion Module becomes the entry point for data acquisition. When data is required, it triggers the appropriate collector package, which retrieves and processes the required source data and stores all information and artifacts needed by the downstream workflows in the TERRA persistence layer.

The target execution flow is: 

Request data 
    -> Trigger Data Ingestion Module 
    -> Run collector package 
        -> Store required data in TERRA database/storage 
    -> Workflow requests persisted data from TERRA databases
    -> Workflow executes

This represents a transition away from workflows directly retrieving and processing external data on demand. Instead, data acquisition and persistence are handled by the ingestion layer, while downstream workflows consume the already-ingested and stored data they require.

In practice, the responsibilities become:

Collector package -> acquire and prepare source data

Data Ingestion Module -> orchestrate collection and persistence

TERRA database/storage -> provide the persisted source of truth

Workflow -> retrieve required persisted data and execute its domain-specific processing

The collector package should therefore persist all data, metadata, references, and artifacts necessary for the corresponding workflow to operate without needing to repeat the original external data-acquisition process.

A more in deapth target separation is:

External caller
  -> Data Ingestion Module HTTP endpoint
  -> validated ingestion profile
  -> application adapter
  -> independently installed collector package
    -> external provider requests
    -> normalization and validation
    -> MongoDB and MinIO persistence
    -> structured collection result
  -> ingestion HTTP response

The ingestion application should not contain provider API calls, provider credentials, response parsing, domain transformations, or collector persistence logic. Those responsibilities belong in the independent package. The ingestion application validates and routes requests, invokes the package, and translates its result or exceptions into an HTTP response.

The current reference implementation is maintained in the collector subdirectory of terra-horizon/uc1.forecaster.uth.alpha. This application pins that subdirectory as the terra-data-collection Git dependency and imports it as data_collection.

docs.title: 1. How the ingestion module calls the current collector
docs.text:
The external entry point is:

POST /api/ingestion/run
Content-Type: application/json

A representative request is:

{
  "run_job_id": "job-sperchios-20260831-001",
  "triggered_at": "2026-08-31T10:00:00+03:00",
  "provider": "sentinel-2",
  "profile": "forecaster-collector",
  "aoi_id": "sperchios",
  "bbox": [22.433493, 38.837552, 22.569555, 38.894223],
  "run_name": "sperchios",
  "history_start": "2016-01-01",
  "target_date": "2026-08-31",
  "mode": "auto",
  "max_days_per_run": 1
}

The current call chain is:

app/api/routes/ingestion.py
  -> execute_ingestion_profile(request)
  -> PROFILE_RUNNERS[request.profile]
  -> run_sentinel_ingestion(config)
  -> data_collection.collect(CollectionRequest(...))
  -> CollectionResult.to_dict()

docs.title: HTTP validation
docs.text:
app/schemas/ingestion.py defines IngestionRunRequest. FastAPI/Pydantic validates the external request before any collector code runs.

The current schema accepts only:

provider = "sentinel-2"
profile  = "forecaster-collector"

Therefore, a new team package is not automatically callable just because its directory exists under app/packages. The application must explicitly approve its provider/profile and register an adapter.

docs.title: Profile selection
docs.text:
app/services/ingestion.py contains the server-controlled registry:

PROFILE_RUNNERS = {
    "forecaster-collector": run_sentinel_ingestion,
}

The caller selects an approved profile name. It cannot supply a Python module, function name, shell command, or arbitrary import path.

The service converts the validated Pydantic request into JSON-compatible data and runs the synchronous adapter in a thread pool:

async def execute_ingestion_profile(request: IngestionRunRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
    runner = PROFILE_RUNNERS[request.profile]
    config = request.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
    return await run_in_threadpool(runner, config)

This keeps long-running provider and storage work off the FastAPI event loop.

docs.title: Application adapter
docs.text:
app/adapters/collector.py is the boundary between the ingestion application and the independent package. Its essential behavior is:

from data_collection import CollectionRequest, collect


def run_sentinel_ingestion(config: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    request = CollectionRequest(
        aoi_id=str(config["aoi_id"]),
        aoi_bbox=list(config["bbox"]),
        run_name=str(config["run_name"]),
        output_root=Path("outputs"),
        history_start=str(config.get("history_start", "2016-01-01")),
        target_date=str(config.get("target_date") or current_utc_date()),
        mode=str(config.get("mode", "auto")),
        max_days_per_run=config.get("max_days_per_run"),
        max_tiles_per_run=config.get("max_tiles_per_run"),
        publish=True,
    )
    result = collect(request)
    return result.to_dict()

The adapter also:

  • prevents concurrent collection for the same aoi_id within the API process;
  • maps collector configuration errors to controlled application errors;
  • maps MongoDB/MinIO connection failures to service-unavailable errors;
  • hides internal tracebacks from HTTP clients;
  • preserves a collector result with status="partial" as a valid HTTP response.

docs.title: Package entry point
docs.text:
The package exports this interface from data_collection/__init__.py:

from .models import CollectionRequest, CollectionResult
from .service import CollectionService, collect

__all__ = ["CollectionRequest", "CollectionResult", "CollectionService", "collect"]

The application uses only:

def collect(request: CollectionRequest) -> CollectionResult:
    ...

The application does not call the provider directly and does not interpret raw provider responses.

docs.title: 2. Target architecture for each collaborating team
docs.text:
Each team should deliver a separately installable package with a unique Python import namespace.

Example:

app/packages/<team-collector>/
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── DATA_CONTRACT.md
├── <team_collection>/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── models.py
│   ├── service.py
│   ├── provider.py
│   ├── normalization.py
│   ├── validation.py
│   ├── remote_storage.py
│   └── schemas/
│       ├── collection-result.schema.json
│       └── observation.schema.json
└── tests/
    ├── test_service.py
    ├── test_provider.py
    └── test_remote_storage.py

The package should expose:

from <team_collection> import CollectionRequest, CollectionResult, collect

with:

def collect(request: CollectionRequest) -> CollectionResult:
    ...

The exact import name for a new team package is not defined by the current collector contract. It must be unique and agreed during integration. A side-by-side collector should not also claim the data_collection namespace.

docs.title: 3. Moving existing collection requests into the package
docs.text: The most important transition is to move provider communication out of the ingestion application or team-specific wrapper scripts and behind the package's collect() entry point.

docs.title: Before transition
docs.text:
A team may currently have logic similar to:

HTTP/controller/scheduler
  -> build provider URL and headers
  -> send request
  -> parse provider response
  -> transform values
  -> write files or database rows

This tightly couples the external provider to the caller.

docs.title: After transition
docs.text:
The desired ownership is:

Ingestion adapter
  -> build typed CollectionRequest
  -> team_collection.collect(request)

Team package
  -> provider discovery/request construction
  -> authentication and retry policy
  -> provider response parsing
  -> normalization and validation
  -> idempotent persistence
  -> CollectionResult

docs.title: Step 1: inventory the existing request
docs.text:
For every existing provider request, document:

  • provider endpoint;
  • HTTP method;
  • authentication mechanism;
  • required identifiers;
  • spatial inputs;
  • time interval inputs;
  • pagination;
  • rate limits and retry rules;
  • response format;
  • how genuine no-data is represented;
  • how transient provider failure is represented;
  • output files or database writes;
  • current duplicate-prevention logic.

Do not expose secrets, tokens, provider headers, or provider-specific response structures in the ingestion HTTP API unless they are genuinely caller-controlled business inputs.

docs.title: Step 2: define the typed package request
docs.text:
Convert caller-controlled business inputs into a dataclass or equivalent typed model.

Example:

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CollectionRequest:
    dataset_id: str
    run_name: str
    start_date: str
    target_date: str
    mode: str = "auto"
    max_units_per_run: int | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.mode not in {"auto", "backfill", "incremental"}:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported collection mode")
        if self.max_units_per_run is not None and self.max_units_per_run < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_units_per_run must be positive")

Use names appropriate to the team's domain. AOI bounding boxes and tiles are required only when the source/domain actually uses them.

The package request must not contain:

  • MongoDB passwords;
  • MinIO secrets;
  • provider client secrets;
  • access tokens;
  • arbitrary executable code;
  • arbitrary module or function paths.

docs.title: Step 3: isolate provider communication
docs.text:
Move all provider-specific request construction and response parsing into a provider client.

class ProviderClient:
    @classmethod
    def from_env(cls) -> "ProviderClient":
        ...

    def discover(self, start_date: str, end_date: str) -> list[SourceUnit]:
        ...

    def fetch(self, source_unit: SourceUnit) -> ProviderResponse:
        ...

This layer owns:

  • API URLs;
  • provider authentication;
  • request payloads and headers;
  • pagination;
  • provider timeouts;
  • bounded retries;
  • rate-limit handling;
  • provider response decoding.

It should return structured Python values to the service, not write directly into FastAPI responses.

docs.title: Step 4: add a collection service
docs.text:
The service coordinates the complete run:

def collect(request: CollectionRequest) -> CollectionResult:
    store = CollectorStore.from_env(dataset_id=request.dataset_id)
    provider = ProviderClient.from_env()
    run_id = create_run_id()

    store.initialize()
    try:
        store.record_run(run_id, status="running", request=request)

        discovered = provider.discover(
            start_date=request.start_date,
            end_date=request.target_date,
        )
        pending = store.find_missing_units(discovered)

        if request.max_units_per_run is not None:
            pending = pending[:request.max_units_per_run]

        collected = []
        failed = []

        for source_unit in pending:
            try:
                raw = provider.fetch(source_unit)
                normalized = normalize_and_validate(raw, source_unit)
                artifact = store.publish_canonical(normalized)
                store.upsert_observation(
                    normalized,
                    artifact=artifact,
                    run_id=run_id,
                )
                collected.append(source_unit.id)
            except RetryableProviderError as exc:
                failed.append({
                    "unit_id": source_unit.id,
                    "retryable": True,
                    "code": exc.code,
                    "message": str(exc),
                })

        result = CollectionResult(
            status="partial" if failed else "success",
            run_id=run_id,
            run_summary=build_summary(collected, failed),
            discovered_units=[unit.id for unit in discovered],
            collected_units=collected,
            failed_units=failed,
        )
        store.record_run(run_id, status=result.status, result=result)
        return result
    except Exception as exc:
        store.record_failed_run(run_id, exc)
        raise
    finally:
        store.close()

The example illustrates the architecture only. Provider-specific discovery, units, transformations, and schemas remain team-owned.

docs.title: Step 5: distinguish failure from genuine no data
docs.text:
The package must make this distinction explicit:

Timeout, authentication error, rate limit, provider 5xx
  -> retryable failed unit
  -> do not write a terminal no-data observation

Valid provider response proving no data exists
  -> terminal unavailable/no-data observation
  -> may be persisted idempotently

Do not convert request failure into zeros, empty measurements, or a successful observation. Missing numeric values must be JSON null, not NaN or infinity.

docs.title: Step 6: make writes idempotent
docs.text:
Define a stable logical identity for every collected record.

The reference observation identity is:

aoi_id + tile_id + observation_date

Another domain may use:

dataset_id + station_id + observation_timestamp

or another documented compound key. The exact identity for another domain is not defined by the current collector contract, but it must be stable and must prevent duplicates when a run is retried.

docs.title: 4. Package output returned to ingestion
docs.text:
The package should return orchestration metadata, not the complete collected dataset.

A common result model should contain at least:

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CollectionResult:
    status: str
    run_id: str
    run_summary: str
    discovered_units: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    collected_units: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    failed_units: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    artifacts: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

Status meanings should be explicit:

Status Meaning success Invocation completed without retryable failed units partial Some work completed, but one or more units remain retryable dry_run Planning/discovery completed without persistence, if supported

The result may include diagnostic local paths, but local paths are container-specific implementation details. Durable consumers should use MongoDB identifiers and MinIO artifact references.

The reference API wraps the package result in:

{
  "run_job_id": "caller-owned-job-id",
  "provider": "approved-provider",
  "profile": "approved-profile",
  "aoi_id": "stable-dataset-id",
  "triggered_at": "2026-08-31T10:00:00+03:00",
  "started_at": "2026-08-31T07:00:01Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-08-31T07:01:15Z",
  "duration_ms": 74000,
  "status": "partial",
  "collector_result": {
    "status": "partial",
    "run_id": "collector-run-...",
    "run_summary": "80 units persisted; 2 remain retryable",
    "discovered_units": ["..."],
    "collected_units": ["..."],
    "failed_units": [
      {
        "unit_id": "...",
        "retryable": true,
        "code": "PROVIDER_REQUEST_FAILED",
        "message": "Provider request failed"
      }
    ],
    "artifacts": [],
    "warnings": []
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Persistence ownership
docs.text:
In the current architecture, the collector package owns MongoDB and MinIO persistence. The ingestion application does not expose a shared persistence service to collector packages.

Until a shared abstraction is introduced, a team package must either:

  1. implement its persistence inside the package following the established conventions; or
  2. use an explicitly approved shared library if one is introduced later.

Teams must not assume the ingestion route will persist returned domain records.

docs.title: MongoDB responsibilities
docs.text:
Use MongoDB for queryable records and current state, such as:

  • normalized observations;
  • stable collection units or geometry definitions;
  • incremental checkpoints;
  • pipeline run lifecycle and result metadata.

The reference collections are:

observations
tiles
collection_state
pipeline_runs

These exact names are mandatory only when producing the existing UC1 collector/forecaster contract. Collection names for unrelated domains require agreement with the consuming application.

Each document should preserve:

  • stable dataset/AOI identifier;
  • stable domain-record identifier;
  • collector run ID;
  • schema version;
  • creation and update timestamps;
  • provider provenance;
  • MinIO artifact reference, when applicable.

Use UTC ISO timestamps and preserve created_at during upsert while updating updated_at.

docs.title: MinIO responsibilities
docs.text:
Use MinIO/S3 for canonical JSON, GeoJSON, large source-derived artifacts, manifests, and run logs.

The reference namespace is:

terra-uc1/<aoi_id>/aoi/...
terra-uc1/<aoi_id>/observations/...
terra-uc1/<aoi_id>/runs/<run_id>/...

A different domain should receive an agreed namespace rather than placing unrelated records under terra-uc1.

docs.title: MongoDB-to-MinIO reference
docs.text:
MongoDB documents should reference their corresponding MinIO object explicitly:

{
  "artifact": {
    "bucket": "terra-data",
    "key": "<namespace>/<dataset-id>/observations/<unit-id>.json",
    "sha256": "<64-character SHA-256>",
    "content_type": "application/json"
  }
}

Use stable object keys and SHA-256 checksums. Before uploading a stable object, compare its checksum with the existing object metadata where possible. MongoDB writes should use stable selectors and upsert=True semantics.

docs.title: Run lifecycle
docs.text:
The package should:

  1. generate a unique collector run_id;
  2. write pipeline_runs.status="running" before collection;
  3. collect and publish data;
  4. update the same run to success or partial;
  5. attempt to update it to failed when an unexpected exception occurs and MongoDB remains reachable.

The caller-owned run_job_id and collector-generated run_id are different identifiers and should not be conflated.

docs.title: 6. Adding a new package to the ingestion application
Step 1: install the package
docs.text:
The root application declares the reference collector as a PEP 508 direct Git dependency in pyproject.toml. The full commit SHA makes installation reproducible, while subdirectory=collector tells pip to build and install only that package directory. Pip may still clone repository data temporarily; the other directories are not installed or added to this repository:

"terra-data-collection @ git+https://github.com/terra-horizon/uc1.forecaster.uth.alpha.git@<full-commit-sha>#subdirectory=collector"

Another team package should use the same pinned dependency form when its source is a packageable subdirectory of a separate repository:

"team-collector-distribution @ git+https://github.com/<organization>/<repository>.git@<full-commit-sha>#subdirectory=<package-directory>"

The application image installs Git before pip install ., allowing pip to fetch these VCS dependencies during the image build. The package must support the application's Python 3.12 runtime and declare all dependencies in its own pyproject.toml. Private repositories additionally require an approved build credential mechanism; credentials must not be embedded in the dependency URL.

docs.title: Step 2: define validated HTTP input
docs.text:
If the new collector uses the same existing request fields, extend the approved provider and profile literal values.

If it requires materially different inputs, add a provider/profile-specific validated Pydantic request model or discriminated union. Do not replace validation with an unrestricted dict[str, Any] payload.

The current application does not yet define this generic multi-provider schema. It must be designed as part of onboarding the first collector whose inputs do not fit IngestionRunRequest.

docs.title: Step 3: add an adapter
docs.text:
Create an application adapter that imports the package and maps validated HTTP fields into its typed request:

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Mapping

from team_collection import CollectionRequest, collect


def run_team_ingestion(config: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    request = CollectionRequest(
        dataset_id=str(config["dataset_id"]),
        run_name=str(config["run_name"]),
        start_date=str(config["start_date"]),
        target_date=str(config["target_date"]),
        max_units_per_run=config.get("max_units_per_run"),
    )
    result = collect(request)
    return result.to_dict()

The adapter may translate application vocabulary into package vocabulary, but it must not contain:

  • external provider requests;
  • authentication logic;
  • provider response parsing;
  • domain calculations;
  • MongoDB observation writes;
  • MinIO object uploads.

docs.title: Step 4: register the profile
docs.text:
Register the adapter in the server-controlled registry:

PROFILE_RUNNERS = {
    "forecaster-collector": run_sentinel_ingestion,
    "team-collector": run_team_ingestion,
}

Also add the profile/provider to the validated schema. Registration must be explicit; package discovery by filesystem scanning is not part of the current architecture.

docs.title: Step 5: map exceptions
docs.text:
The adapter should translate package-specific exceptions into the application's controlled categories:

invalid package configuration -> HTTP 400
same dataset already running  -> HTTP 409
MongoDB/MinIO unavailable      -> HTTP 503
unexpected execution failure  -> HTTP 500 without traceback
partial collection result      -> HTTP 200 with status="partial"

Provider failures affecting individual units should normally be reported in failed_units, not raised as an application-wide exception when the run can safely continue.

docs.title: 7. Configuration and secrets
docs.text:
Provider and storage configuration must be supplied through environment variables or an approved secret manager.

Each package should document:

  • required provider URL/configuration;
  • provider client ID/secret or API key;
  • optional fallback credentials;
  • MongoDB URI requirements;
  • MinIO endpoint, bucket, access key and secret;
  • TLS verification and custom CA configuration.

Secrets must never be:

  • hardcoded in source;
  • committed in .env files;
  • included in HTTP requests;
  • written into collection results;
  • persisted in pipeline metadata;
  • printed in logs.

Prefer environment variables injected by Docker/Kubernetes. The reference package's local .env search is useful for standalone development, but production packages should not override already injected environment variables.

docs.title: 8. Logging and error behavior
docs.text:
Use structured logs containing:

timestamp
level
collector/component
run_id
dataset_id or aoi_id
phase
unit_id when applicable
message

Required failure behavior:

Situation Package behavior Provider timeout/network error Bounded retry, then retryable failed unit Authentication failure Bounded credential handling; never log secrets Rate limit Respect Retry-After where available and use bounded backoff Provider 5xx Retryable failure unless provider contract states otherwise Invalid response Validation/parsing failure; do not fabricate values Genuine no data Terminal no-data record using null values MongoDB/MinIO preflight failure Fail before expensive collection work Duplicate data Idempotent update/no-op Unexpected exception Record failed run where possible, close clients, re-raise

Do not copy the reference mixture of print() and JSONL logging. New packages should route provider and service messages through one structured logging system.

docs.title: 9. Minimum package tests
docs.text:
Before delivery, each package should provide tests for:

  • public CollectionRequest, CollectionResult, and collect imports;
  • request validation;
  • first successful collection;
  • normalization and schema validation;
  • incremental rerun without duplicates;
  • stable MongoDB upsert selectors;
  • MinIO key generation and checksum metadata;
  • provider pagination, timeout and invalid response behavior;
  • retryable failure followed by successful resume;
  • genuine no-data handling with JSON nulls;
  • partial result reporting;
  • pipeline run lifecycle;
  • storage-client cleanup;
  • credential redaction;
  • adapter mapping from HTTP request to package request;
  • controlled HTTP error responses;
  • successful installation and import in the Python 3.12 application image.

Tests should use fake provider and storage implementations. Live-provider tests should be opt-in and use non-production credentials.

docs.title: Extract the collector
docs.text:
• [ ] Existing provider requests are inventoried.
  • [ ] Provider calls have been removed from controllers, routes and schedulers.
  • [ ] An independently installable package exists.
  • [ ] The package has a unique Python import namespace.
  • [ ] CollectionRequest, CollectionResult, and collect() are public.
  • [ ] Provider communication is isolated behind a client/service.
  • [ ] Normalization and validation occur inside the package.
  • [ ] Retryable failure and genuine no data are distinct.
  • [ ] Stable record identities are documented.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
• [ ] MongoDB collections and unique keys are agreed.
  • [ ] MinIO namespace and object keys are agreed.
  • [ ] MongoDB documents reference MinIO artifacts.
  • [ ] References include bucket, key, SHA-256 and content type.
  • [ ] Upserts and uploads are idempotent.
  • [ ] Pipeline run lifecycle is persisted.
  • [ ] Local files are treated as staging, not durable external contracts.

docs.title: Ingestion integration
docs.text:
• [ ] Package is installed by the root image.
  • [ ] HTTP input is validated by Pydantic.
  • [ ] An application adapter constructs the package request.
  • [ ] Provider/profile is explicitly registered.
  • [ ] Collector runs in the thread pool.
  • [ ] Adapter exceptions map to controlled HTTP errors.
  • [ ] Partial results remain HTTP-successful structured responses.

docs.title: Security and quality
docs.text:
• [ ] No credentials are hardcoded.
  • [ ] Secrets are not logged, returned or persisted.
  • [ ] Dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml.
  • [ ] Package runs under Python 3.12.
  • [ ] Tests do not require live services by default.
  • [ ] README and data contract document the delivered behavior.

docs.title: 11. Current-contract limitations teams must know
docs.text:
The following are not generic capabilities of the current application and require explicit integration work:

  • automatic discovery of packages placed under app/packages;
  • arbitrary provider/profile registration by the caller;
  • a shared application-level collector interface or abstract base class;
  • a shared application-level MongoDB/MinIO persistence service;
  • a generic multi-provider HTTP request schema;
  • common domain-record fields for sources that are not UC1 observations;
  • common MongoDB collection names for unrelated domains;
  • common MinIO namespaces for unrelated domains;
  • generic scheduling or late-arriving-data policy.

These items are not defined by the current collector contract. Teams should not invent incompatible solutions independently; they should agree them with the ingestion-module maintainers during package onboarding.

docs.title: 12. Rules that are mandatory versus recommended
Mandatory for integration
docs.text:
• Deliver an installable package, not loose scripts copied into the ingestion application.
  • Expose a typed request, structured result, and one callable collection entry point.
  • Add a server-side adapter and explicit profile/provider registration.
  • Keep provider requests and business transformations inside the package.
  • Validate inputs and normalized records.
  • Distinguish retryable failures from genuine no data.
  • Define stable identifiers and idempotent persistence.
  • Use MongoDB/MinIO according to an agreed data contract.
  • Return status/references rather than complete provider payloads.
  • Supply configuration through environment variables or an approved secret manager.
  • Declare dependencies and support the hosting runtime.
  • Provide automated tests.

docs.title: Recommended implementation patterns
docs.text:
• Match the reference separation into models, service, provider, validation and storage modules.
  • Use dependency injection for provider and storage clients.
  • Ship JSON Schemas as package data.
  • Maintain local staging artifacts for recovery and diagnosis.
  • Use deterministic JSON and SHA-256 checksums.
  • Keep a resumable collection checkpoint.
  • Provide a standalone CLI and optional standalone container.
  • Use structured logging throughout.
  • Store the effective request and package/schema version with every pipeline run.

docs.title: Reference-specific behavior not to copy blindly
docs.text:
• Sentinel-specific STAC calls and evalscripts;
  • river extraction and tile generation;
  • UC1 water-quality metric names;
  • the terra-uc1 namespace for unrelated domains;
  • unused Sentinel-3/image collector classes;
  • mutable defaults such as bbox=[];
  • direct print() logging;
  • ambiguous use of collected for terminal unavailable records;
  • strict non-overlapping discovery without a late-arrival lookback policy;
  • returning operating-system-specific local paths as durable references.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
For the coastal-uc3-sentinel2 package, local wheel installation and independent runtime settings, see UC3 integration. Supply its wheel in vendor/ before installing the application or building its Docker image.

The FastAPI layer does not maintain the collector package needed for the forecaster. It passes the request to the installed collector package, which reads storage and CDSE configuration from the process environment. Copy .env.example to .env and never commit the populated file.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Required Purpose DATA_COLLECTION_ENV_FILE No Optional explicit collector environment-file path. MONGO_URI Yes Full MongoDB URI including database and, when required, authSource. MINIO_ENDPOINT Yes MinIO S3 API URL. Use port 9000, not the console port 9001. MINIO_ACCESS_KEY Yes MinIO application/root user for the current local stack. MINIO_SECRET_KEY Yes Matching MinIO secret. MINIO_BUCKET_NAME Yes Existing bucket used by the collector. MINIO_VERIFY_TLS No Enables TLS certificate verification; defaults to true. MINIO_CA_BUNDLE No Optional CA bundle path for private certificate authorities. CDSE_CLIENT_ID Yes Primary CDSE OAuth client ID. CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET Yes Primary CDSE OAuth client secret. CDSE_BACKUP_CLIENT_ID, CDSE_BACKUP_CLIENT_SECRET No First backup credential pair. CDSE_BACKUP_2_* through CDSE_BACKUP_9_* No Additional ordered backup pairs.

The database name is taken from MONGO_URI; a separate MONGO_DATABASE value is not used by the collector.

docs.title: Local host execution
docs.text:
When Uvicorn runs directly on Windows and MongoDB/MinIO publish their standard ports to the host, endpoints may use loopback:

MONGO_URI=mongodb://<user>:<url-encoded-password>@127.0.0.1:27017/terra_db?authSource=admin
MINIO_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9000

docs.title: Docker execution
docs.text:
Inside a container, localhost, 127.0.0.1, and ::1 identify the API container itself. The application Compose file attaches to the external terra-network, so use Docker DNS names and internal ports:

MONGO_URI=mongodb://<user>:<url-encoded-password>@terra-mongodb:27017/terra_db?authSource=admin
MINIO_ENDPOINT=http://terra-minio:9000

For the provided local stack, source MongoDB and MinIO credentials from: terra-node-stack

docs.title: Applying changes
docs.text:
Compose injects .env when it creates a container. After environment-only changes, recreate without rebuilding:

docker compose up -d --force-recreate

Use --build only after Dockerfile, dependency, or application-source changes.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: For the coastal-uc3-sentinel2 package, local wheel installation and independent runtime settings, see UC3 integration. Supply its wheel in vendor/ before installing the application or building its Docker image.

docs.title: Local Python process
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • Python 3.12+
  • reachable MongoDB and MinIO
  • an existing MinIO bucket
  • valid CDSE client credentials

Install and run:

python -m venv .venv
python -m pip install vendor/terra_wp2_uc3_ingestion-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl -e ".[test]"
uvicorn app.main:app --reload

Installing the application builds and installs only the pinned collector subdirectory from terra-horizon/uc1.forecaster.uth.alpha. Pip may clone the source repository into a temporary directory while resolving the Git dependency, but no other project directory is installed or retained in this application repository.

The API listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 by default. Swagger UI is at /docs.

docs.title: Docker image
docs.text:
The repository Dockerfile:

  1. starts from python:3.12-slim;
  2. installs Git and CA certificates for the pinned VCS dependency;
  3. copies the FastAPI project;
  4. installs the FastAPI application and its pinned collector dependency;
  5. starts Uvicorn on 0.0.0.0:8000.

Build directly:

docker build -t data-ingestion-module:local .

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
The application Compose file deploys only the API. MongoDB and MinIO remain owned by the separately supplied TERRA node stack.

Expected resources:

terra-network
  - terra-mongodb:27017
  - terra-minio:9000
  - data-ingestion-module:8000

Start the node stack first, then run:

docker compose up --build -d
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f data-ingestion-module

Stop only the API container with:

docker compose down

Because terra-network is external, bringing down this Compose project does not remove MongoDB, MinIO, or their network.

docs.title: Persistent data
docs.text:
MongoDB and MinIO are the durable stores. The current API Compose service does not mount outputs/ as a volume, so local collector staging files disappear when its container is replaced. On the next run, the collector hydrates remote observations, collection state, and tile artifacts before calculating work.

The collector's CDSE discovery cache is local and is not restored from remote storage. It is recreated only when a discovery window actually runs.

docs.title: What does profile select?
docs.text: It selects a server-registered process adapter: forecaster-collector invokes the UC1 collector, and coastal-uc3-sentinel2 invokes the UC3 package. See UC3 integration for its request and deployment settings. Arbitrary commands and module names are not accepted.

docs.title: Does the endpoint run in the background?
docs.text: No. It waits for the selected profile to finish. The blocking collector runs in a worker thread, but the HTTP request remains open.
