docs.title: Pipeline Test Scenarios
docs.text: These scenarios exercise the implemented FastAPI-to-collector flow. Use a test AOI and local MongoDB/MinIO data that can be reset safely.

docs.title: Scenario 1: Request validation
docs.text:
Remove profile, provide an unknown profile, remove the timezone from triggered_at, or reverse bbox coordinates.

Expected result: HTTP 422; the collector is not called.

docs.title: Scenario 2: First bounded backfill
docs.text:
Use a new aoi_id and run_name with:

{
  "mode": "auto",
  "max_days_per_run": 1,
  "max_tiles_per_run": 1
}

Expected result:

  • CDSE discovery windows are requested and written under outputs/<run>/cdse_stac_cache;
  • river tiles are generated;
  • at most one date and one tile are processed;
  • MongoDB and MinIO receive collector-owned data;
  • HTTP status is 200 with collector status success or partial.

docs.title: Scenario 3: Incremental rerun
docs.text:
Repeat the same AOI after a successful run.

Expected result:

  • remote state and observations are restored if local staging is absent;
  • completed tile/date units are not duplicated;
  • only newly available or incomplete work is selected.

docs.title: Scenario 4: Local output deletion
docs.text:
Delete only the test run's local outputs/<run> directory and rerun the same AOI.

Expected result: MongoDB/MinIO state is hydrated. Historical CDSE requests are not repeated when restored state already covers the target date. The local STAC cache may remain absent when discovery window count is zero.

docs.title: Scenario 5: Partial run
docs.text:
Cause one collector unit to fail transiently while another succeeds.

Expected result: HTTP 200, response status partial, successful data remains published, and retryable units appear in failed_units.

docs.title: Scenario 6: MongoDB connectivity and authentication
docs.text:
Test an unreachable hostname, then a URI without credentials against an authenticated MongoDB.

Expected result: unreachable storage maps to HTTP 503. An authorization error during later MongoDB setup may surface as the collector's generic HTTP 500; inspect container logs and pipeline_runs during diagnosis.

docs.title: Scenario 7: MinIO connectivity
docs.text:
Set MINIO_ENDPOINT to localhost inside the API container.

Expected result: HTTP 503. Restore http://terra-minio:9000, recreate the API container, and confirm the bucket and credentials match the node stack.

docs.title: Scenario 8: Same-AOI concurrency
docs.text:
Send two overlapping requests for the same AOI to one API process.

Expected result: one request runs and the other returns HTTP 409.

docs.title: Scenario 9: Independent AOIs
docs.text:
Send requests for two different AOI IDs.

Expected result: the process-local guard allows both. Resource capacity and external API limits still apply.

docs.title: Scenario 10: Container replacement
docs.text:
Run successfully, recreate the API container, and run the same AOI again.

Expected result: local staging starts empty, durable collector state is restored, and only required incremental work runs.

docs.title: Automated API tests
docs.text:
Run from the repository root:

python -m pytest

The FastAPI tests use httpx.ASGITransport and mock the collector boundary. They verify:

  • liveness and readiness response contracts;
  • sanitized HTTP 503 readiness responses;
  • HTTP 200 success responses;
  • partial collector results;
  • orchestration metadata and selected profile;
  • construction of the collector request;
  • timezone, AOI, bounding-box, and profile validation;
  • stable, sanitized HTTP 500 behavior for unexpected collector errors.

These tests do not contact CDSE, MongoDB, or MinIO.

docs.title: Collector package tests
docs.text:
The collector's unit tests are owned and run in its source repository. This repository tests the installed package at the adapter boundary:

python -m pip install vendor/terra_wp2_uc3_ingestion-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl -e ".[test]"
python -m pytest

The owning collector repository is responsible for its incremental-state, discovery-cache, retry, storage-publication, and schema-validation tests.

docs.title: Manual API test
docs.text:
Start Uvicorn or the Compose service and execute tests_external/ingestion.http. For a commissioning run, retain small limits:

{
  "max_days_per_run": 1,
  "max_tiles_per_run": 1
}

Confirm:

  1. HTTP status is 200 for success or partial.
  2. The response echoes run_job_id, provider, profile, and AOI.
  3. MongoDB pipeline_runs contains the collector run.
  4. Observation/tile/state documents are present under the expected AOI.
  5. MinIO contains stable AOI artifacts and a run-scoped prefix.

docs.title: Failure-path checks
docs.text:
Test Expected result Missing or unknown profile HTTP 422. Timestamp without timezone HTTP 422. Reversed or incomplete bbox HTTP 422. Missing collector environment variable HTTP 400. MongoDB/MinIO unreachable HTTP 503. Concurrent request for same AOI in one API process HTTP 409. Unexpected collector exception HTTP 500 without a traceback in the response.

Use container logs and the collector's pipeline_runs records for internal diagnostics. Public errors intentionally avoid returning tracebacks.

docs.title: UC3 package integration
docs.text: POST /api/ingestion/run accepts profile: "coastal-uc3-sentinel2". The dispatcher calls app/adapters/uc3.py in the existing thread pool. The adapter passes the canonical profile through unchanged and invokes wp2_uc3_ingestion.profile.run_profile. It strips UC1-only options and preserves the package result. There is no additional service or job queue.

docs.title: Build and install
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12 and the application virtual environment. From the application root, build the wheel from the supplied UC3 project root, not its Python package subdirectory (set <UC3_SOURCE_ROOT> to the authorised local source location):

.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir vendor "<UC3_SOURCE_ROOT>"
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install vendor/terra_wp2_uc3_ingestion-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl -e ".[test]"
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip check
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "from wp2_uc3_ingestion.profile import run_profile; from wp2_uc3_ingestion.contract import load_schema; from wp2_uc3_ingestion.requests_builder import load_authorised_aois; print(load_schema('acquisition_request')['title']); print(len(load_authorised_aois()['aois']))"

For future upgrades, obtain the team's official wheel or its complete source distribution metadata with the source handoff; do not assume the current local packaging scaffold represents future package metadata. The wheel includes schemas, examples and the AOI registry. No private GitHub access is needed at build time when the authorised wheel is supplied. The existing UC1 dependency still uses its own Git URL.

If the pip build frontend stalls, the installed setuptools backend can build the copied source without downloading build tools. From build/uc3-source/:

..\..\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import setuptools.build_meta; print(setuptools.build_meta.build_wheel('../../vendor'))"

The application pins terra-wp2-uc3-ingestion==0.5.1. This release changes the CDSE catalogue request's Accept header to application/geo+json, which the catalogue endpoint requires. The catalogue URL remains the package's official default. UC3's dependency ranges allow UC1's pinned pymongo, requests and python-dotenv versions. Do not apply the team's standalone constraints-py312.txt wholesale: its pins differ from UC1's. Resolve the wheel and application together and run pip check.

docs.title: Docker and upgrades
docs.text:
Place the wheel in vendor/ before docker build -t data-ingestion-module:uc3 .. The Dockerfile installs libexpat1 for rasterio and resolves the application and the explicitly named local wheel together. It does not embed desktop paths. CI must obtain the wheel through private build-artifact delivery; a Git checkout alone does not contain it. Wheels and the copied source under build/ are ignored.

For a new handover, rebuild from its project root, check the wheel's version and resources, update the application dependency pin and Dockerfile wheel filename, and supply that artifact to CI. Repeat import/resource checks, dependency checks, the complete test suite and a Docker build before deployment. Keep the prior wheel in private artifact storage for rollback.

docs.title: Runtime configuration
docs.text:
Use the UC3_INGEST_* placeholders in the root .env.example. UC3 never falls back to UC1's MONGO_URI, MINIO_* or CDSE_* values. Supply variables to the process, Docker --env-file, Compose env_file, or Uvicorn --env-file .env. The Python entry point itself does not load .env; do not depend on UC1 loading it.

Required settings are PROJECT_ID, CDSE_CLIENT_ID/CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET (or supported credential files/backup pairs), MONGODB_URI, MONGODB_DATABASE, MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_SECRET_KEY, MINIO_BUCKET and MINIO_PREFIX, all prefixed with UC3_INGEST_. Additional settings include MONGODB_COLLECTION_PREFIX, MINIO_REGION, MINIO_SECURE, MINIO_CERT_CHECK, ALLOW_SERVING_NAMESPACE, AOI_REGISTRY_FILE, WORK_DIR, and CDSE URL overrides. Omit WORK_DIR to use temporary working files cleaned up by the package.

The intended shared deployment uses database terra-db, collection prefix uc3_, bucket terra-bucket, and object prefix terra-uc3. The package requires UC3_INGEST_ALLOW_SERVING_NAMESPACE=true to publish into this serving namespace; the example deliberately uses test storage with this flag disabled. Credentials must grant access to the configured namespace. PROJECT_ID is required in the environment even when a request includes uc3.project_id.

docs.title: Request and outcomes
docs.text:
{
  "run_job_id": "uc3-aoi02-20261019-001",
  "triggered_at": "2026-10-19T09:00:00Z",
  "provider": "sentinel-2",
  "profile": "coastal-uc3-sentinel2",
  "aoi_id": "aoi_02",
  "bbox": [-2.84437, 56.39264, -2.78475, 56.43782],
  "uc3": {
    "contract_version": 2,
    "mode": "latest",
    "time_from": "2026-09-19T00:00:00Z",
    "time_to": "2026-10-19T00:00:00Z",
    "selection_policy": "uc3_parity_pilot",
    "max_scenes": 1
  }
}

The UC3 object requires version 2, mode (latest or window), and an explicit, timezone-aware increasing time window. Offsets are normalised to UTC by the package. selection_policy defaults to uc3_parity_pilot; the other supported policy is uc3_monthly_backfill. max_scenes is an integer from 1 to 24; omitted, the current policies use 3. Optional package metadata fields are project_id, request_id, registry_version, and window_id. Unknown nested fields are rejected. AOI ID and bbox must match the operator-selected or packaged authorised registry (package tolerance: 0.000001 degrees). They are checked before acquisition. UC3 requires no run_name, history_start, or target_date; those UC1 fields are not forwarded. UC1 still requires run_name and retains its existing defaults.

Result HTTP Meaning completed 200 Acquisition completed; inspect scene IDs and output references. no_data 200 No suitable data; a normal acquisition outcome. failed 200 Structured failure; inspect package error/retry metadata. Invalid request schema 422 Missing/invalid UC3 options or outer fields. Unauthorised AOI or invalid package configuration 400 Acquisition cannot begin. Same UC3 AOI already running in this process 409 Retry after the current invocation completes. UC3 package/runtime unavailable 503 Repair package installation. Unexpected exception or invalid package outcome 500 Masked execution error.

Both top-level status and collector_result.status retain the UC3 outcome. Scene IDs, timestamps, references, and structured failures remain in collector_result. HTTP 200 alone does not establish acquisition success. The request, response and internal package metadata all use coastal-uc3-sentinel2. The former uc3profile name is no longer accepted. Update callers and use /health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2 for UC3 readiness.

Execution is synchronous to the HTTP caller; configure proxy/client timeouts for acquisition duration. The AOI concurrency guard is process-local, not a distributed lock. There is no durable job submission or polling contract in this integration.

docs.title: Readiness and offline tests
docs.text:
GET /health/ready retains the UC1 contract. GET /health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2 independently returns 200 or 503 with package, configuration, mongodb, and minio checks (ok, unavailable, or skipped). It imports the package, reads its schema and registry, checks required settings, pings MongoDB, and lists at most one object under the UC3 scene prefix. It performs no writes or CDSE calls. Credential presence does not prove CDSE authentication, and storage reads do not prove write permissions. UC3 readiness failure does not change UC1 readiness.

.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_uc3_profile.py tests/test_uc3_health.py -q
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q

Tests use the real package for contract translation and resource checks, with acquisition and external services mocked. Live CDSE authentication, download, publication permissions and downstream assimilation require separate validation.

docs.title: Manual test from Windows
docs.text:
The current 0.5.1 wheel must be installed and checked before use; package-level catalogue behavior can be regression-checked offline without making a CDSE request. No live acquisition or production storage access is part of that check.

If Docker cannot read a wheel built by a sandboxed Windows process, reset only that artifact's permissions to inherit from its parent directory, then rebuild:

icacls vendor\terra_wp2_uc3_ingestion-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl /reset

Add the UC3 settings from .env.example to your existing private .env; retain the UC1 values. For a host Python process, use storage addresses reachable from Windows, not container-only DNS names. Start the application from the project root:

.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --env-file .env

In a second terminal:

curl.exe -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/live
curl.exe -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2

Liveness should return 200. UC3 readiness should return 200 with all four checks ok; 503 identifies missing configuration or unavailable dependencies. Readiness does not verify CDSE credentials against the provider or prove storage writes.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs and use POST /api/ingestion/run with the request above, or use tests_external/uc3.http in an HTTP client. Update the run ID, trigger timestamp and acquisition window; retain the authorised bbox. Use max_scenes: 1 for the first acquisition. This POST performs a real download and publishes into the configured UC3 namespace. Inspect status and collector_result, including scene IDs, references and error details; HTTP 200 can also represent no_data or failed.

For a manual Docker run, the configured storage must be reachable from the container. When using the existing TERRA node stack and its external network:

docker run --rm --name uc3-manual --network terra-network --env-file .env -p 127.0.0.1:18001:8000 data-ingestion-module:uc3-test

Use port 18001 for the URLs above. This runs separately from the Compose service on port 18000. Stop the foreground test container with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Deploying the Git checkout on the server
docs.text:
Commit the application, tests, configuration template and documentation. Deliver vendor/terra_wp2_uc3_ingestion-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl separately to the server's checkout via private file transfer or artifact storage: it is Git-ignored, so git pull alone cannot supply it. Alternatively deliver a built application image through a private image registry. Do not commit the wheel, source handover, or .env.

Merge the UC3 variables into the server's existing private .env. The intended shared deployment settings are:

UC3_INGEST_PROJECT_ID=YOUR_UC3_PROJECT_ID
UC3_INGEST_MONGODB_URI=mongodb://APP_USERNAME:URL_ENCODED_PASSWORD\@terra-mongodb:27017/terra-db?authSource=AUTH_DATABASE
UC3_INGEST_MONGODB_DATABASE=terra-db
UC3_INGEST_MONGODB_COLLECTION_PREFIX=uc3_
UC3_INGEST_MINIO_ENDPOINT=http://terra-minio:9000
UC3_INGEST_MINIO_SECURE=false
UC3_INGEST_MINIO_BUCKET=terra-bucket
UC3_INGEST_MINIO_PREFIX=terra-uc3
UC3_INGEST_MINIO_REGION=us-east-1
UC3_INGEST_ALLOW_SERVING_NAMESPACE=true

Also supply UC3_INGEST_CDSE_CLIENT_ID, UC3_INGEST_CDSE_CLIENT_SECRET, UC3_INGEST_MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, and UC3_INGEST_MINIO_SECRET_KEY. The serving namespace flag enables writes into UC3's serving data; use it for the intended production deployment, not an isolated test. Confirm the actual node names, Mongo authentication database, project ID, storage permissions and outbound CDSE connectivity with the server configuration. Keep UC1 settings unchanged.

Once the wheel, environment and existing terra-network are present, from the server checkout:

docker compose build data-ingestion-module
docker compose up -d --no-deps data-ingestion-module
docker compose logs --tail=100 data-ingestion-module
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18000/health/live
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18000/health/ready
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18000/health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2

The current Compose file binds port 18000 only to server loopback. Retain the existing reverse-proxy mapping for /data-ingestion/; the public UC3 readiness URL is https://server.iprism.eu/data-ingestion/health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2 and the POST URL remains https://server.iprism.eu/data-ingestion/api/ingestion/run. Ensure the proxy's access controls cover ingestion and its timeouts accommodate synchronous acquisition; the application adds no UC3 API-key mechanism. Keep the previous image for rollback. No additional UC3 service, job-store provisioning, or storage migration is required by this package integration.

docs.title: Private package and distribution disclaimer
docs.text:
The terra-wp2-uc3-ingestion package is developed and maintained by the UC3 team in a private repository. Its source code and wheel are not included in this repository and must be obtained through an authorised handover or approved private artifact distribution channel. A Git checkout alone is insufficient to build or deploy the integration without the required wheel.

This repository documents and maintains the integration with that external dependency; it does not claim ownership of the UC3 package or grant rights to use, modify, publish, or redistribute it beyond those authorised by its maintainers and applicable licensing terms. Package updates, upstream defects, and distribution permissions should be coordinated with the UC3 team.

docs.title: Ingestion Workflow
docs.text:
The Data Ingestion Module provides a unified API for executing ingestion workflows through registered collection profiles.

Currently supported profiles:

  • UC1 — forecaster-collector: Sentinel-2 statistical data collection for the forecasting pipeline.
  • UC3 — coastal-uc3-sentinel2: Sentinel-2 L2A scene discovery, quality assessment, raster acquisition, and publication through the externally maintained UC3 ingestion package.

Both profiles share the existing FastAPI application, request dispatcher, execution infrastructure, and API response envelope, while maintaining independent collector implementations and configurations.

docs.title: 1. Request validation
docs.text:
The caller sends POST /api/ingestion/run.

Pydantic validates common request fields:

  • A non-empty run_job_id and aoi_id.
  • A timezone-aware triggered_at.
  • provider: sentinel-2.
  • A registered profile.
  • A four-number WGS84 bounding box with ordered coordinates.
  • Profile-specific acquisition parameters and constraints.

UC1 validation

The forecaster-collector profile requires run_name and supports:

  • history_start and target_date.
  • Collection mode.
  • Optional date and tile limits.
  • UC1-specific collection parameters.

UC3 validation

The coastal-uc3-sentinel2 profile requires a dedicated uc3 configuration containing:

  • contract_version: 2.
  • mode: latest or window.
  • time_from and time_to: timezone-aware timestamps defining an increasing acquisition window.
  • selection_policy: defaults to uc3_parity_pilot; uc3_monthly_backfill is also supported.
  • max_scenes: optional integer between 1 and 24.

UC3 additionally validates the AOI identifier and bounding box against its authorised AOI registry. It does not require UC1-specific fields such as run_name, history_start, or target_date.

Invalid request schemas return HTTP 422 before an adapter executes. Package-level AOI authorisation or configuration failures can return HTTP 400.

docs.title: 2. Profile selection
docs.text:
app/services/ingestion.py selects the appropriate registered profile runner.

The current mapping is:

forecaster-collector    -> run_sentinel_ingestion
coastal-uc3-sentinel2   -> UC3 adapter runner

Both collectors use synchronous Python execution. The application executes profile runners in a Starlette worker thread to avoid blocking the FastAPI event loop.

The UC3 integration invokes the external package through:

from wp2_uc3_ingestion.profile import run_profile

result = run_profile(config)

The canonical profile name coastal-uc3-sentinel2 is preserved throughout the UC3 request and response.

No additional UC3 microservice, background job queue, or polling mechanism is introduced.

docs.title: 3. Adapter translation
docs.text:
Each profile uses its own adapter to translate the validated API request into the corresponding collector contract.

UC1 adapter

The adapter converts the validated request into CollectionRequest.

It:

  • Sets output_root to outputs.
  • Passes AOI information, dates, mode, and collection limits.
  • Enables publication of collected results.
  • Applies a process-local guard preventing concurrent collection of the same AOI.

UC3 adapter

The adapter translates the validated request into the external UC3 package's acquisition configuration.

It:

  • Preserves the canonical UC3 profile identifier.
  • Passes the authorised AOI, acquisition time window, selection policy, and scene limits.
  • Excludes UC1-only request options.
  • Invokes run_profile() using the installed UC3 package.
  • Preserves the package's structured acquisition result and error information.

UC3 also uses a process-local AOI concurrency guard.

These guards are not distributed locks and do not coordinate concurrent requests across multiple application instances.

docs.title: 4. Storage preflight and hydration
docs.text: Both profiles perform storage and configuration checks, but their preparation workflows differ.

docs.title: UC1
docs.text:
For a published run, the collector:

  1. Loads runtime environment variables.
  2. Connects to MongoDB and MinIO and checks required storage resources.
  3. Verifies the stable AOI definition.
  4. Restores observations from MongoDB when local history is absent.
  5. Restores collection state and tile artifacts from MinIO when local files are absent.
  6. Creates a pipeline_runs record with collector status running.

docs.title: UC3
docs.text:
The UC3 package uses an independent configuration namespace:

UC3_INGEST_*

Its preparation includes:

  1. Loading and validating UC3-specific settings.
  2. Validating CDSE provider credentials and configured credential pairs.
  3. Checking the configured MongoDB and MinIO storage namespaces.
  4. Verifying the requested AOI against the authorised registry.
  5. Establishing the acquisition configuration, output grid, and publication settings.

UC3 supports a primary CDSE credential and up to four backup credentials, with authentication-based failover, token caching, and retry handling.

UC3 does not use UC1's local observation-history hydration workflow. Its acquisition and publication lifecycle is managed by the external package.

docs.title: UC1 — Statistical collection
docs.text:
The collector calculates discovery windows from mode, history_start, target_date, and restored state.

  • Existing cdse_stac_cache entries are reused when a matching local cache is present.
  • Missing windows are requested from CDSE and cached locally.
  • If state already covers the target date, no discovery request is made.
  • River tiles are restored or generated as needed.
  • Missing tile/date units are collected through the Sentinel Hub Statistical API.
  • Run limits can restrict dates and tiles for commissioning tests.

The collected information supports the UC1 forecasting workflow through satellite-derived statistics and observations.

docs.title: UC3 — Scene discovery and raster acquisition
docs.text:
The UC3 package performs the following sequence:

  1. Catalogue discovery: Queries the CDSE Catalogue API for Sentinel-2 Level-2A scenes intersecting the requested AOI and time interval.
  2. Scene deduplication: Groups catalogue entries belonging to the same satellite acquisition across MGRS tiles.
  3. Catalogue prefiltering: Evaluates scene-level cloud coverage and prepares eligible acquisitions.
  4. AOI quality assessment: Uses the Sentinel Hub Process API to retrieve Scene Classification Layer (SCL) data and evaluates cloud coverage, cloud shadows, no-data pixels, and unusable areas within the AOI.
  5. Scene selection: Rejects scenes that fail the configured quality policy and selects eligible acquisitions according to the requested selection policy.
  6. Raster acquisition: Requests the selected Sentinel-2 imagery through the CDSE Process API.
  7. Raster validation: Verifies raster metadata, required bands, spatial coverage, and preflight quality conditions.
  8. Scene packaging: Constructs the acquisition metadata and corresponding raster artifact for publication.

The UC3 raster contains five Sentinel-2 bands:

B02, B03, B04, B08, B11

Raster data is delivered in GeoTIFF format with Float32 reflectance values.

The max_scenes parameter limits the number of delivered scenes.

UC3 retains acquisition identifiers, observation timestamps, scene quality metrics, processing metadata, and provenance information.

docs.title: UC1 publication
docs.text:
The collector updates local history and state, then publishes:

  • Observation and tile documents to MongoDB.
  • Incremental collection state to MongoDB.
  • Stable AOI, tile, observation, result, input-manifest, and log artifacts to MinIO.
  • The terminal success, partial, or failed pipeline run status.

Partial runs retain successfully collected data and report retryable failures in failed_units.

docs.title: UC3 publication
docs.text:
The UC3 package publishes its acquisition outputs to the configured MongoDB and MinIO infrastructure.

MongoDB stores records associated with:

  • scenes
  • scene_assets
  • artifacts

In shared deployment configurations, these collections use the uc3_ prefix.

MinIO stores the acquired raster artifacts under the configured UC3 object prefix.

Publication records include:

  • Provider scene identifiers and acquisition metadata.
  • Raster characteristics, including dimensions, bands, format, and CRS.
  • AOI quality assessment results.
  • Processing parameters and provenance.
  • Artifact identifiers, object references, sizes, and checksums.
  • Publication state and reuse metadata.

The package reports committed artifacts and their storage references in the acquisition result.

UC3 publication outcomes are:

  • completed: acquisition and publication completed.
  • no_data: no suitable scenes were available.
  • failed: an acquisition, processing, or publication failure occurred.

These statuses remain distinct from the UC1 collector's success, partial, and failed outcomes.

docs.title: 7. API response
docs.text:
FastAPI returns a common response envelope containing:

  • Request job ID.
  • Provider and ingestion profile.
  • AOI identifier.
  • Trigger, start, and completion timestamps.
  • Execution duration.
  • Overall ingestion status.
  • Serialized collector result.

Each profile preserves its specific result structure within collector_result.

UC1 response

Contains the collector's execution status, collected observations, generated artifacts, processing metadata, and any failed collection units.

Collector-local paths refer only to the current host or container.

UC3 response

Contains the package's structured acquisition information, including:

  • Package and contract versions.
  • Catalogue discovery and selection statistics.
  • Candidate scenes and rejection decisions.
  • AOI quality measurements.
  • Delivered scene packages.
  • Raster metadata.
  • MongoDB/MinIO artifact references.
  • Structured failure details and retryability information.

For UC3, HTTP 200 does not necessarily indicate a successful acquisition. The caller must inspect the top-level status and collector_result.status.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Condition HTTP status Invalid request schema 422 Invalid collector configuration or unauthorised AOI 400 Same AOI already running in this process 409 Package/runtime unavailable 503 Unexpected execution failure 500 UC3 completed acquisition 200 UC3 no-data acquisition 200 UC3 structured acquisition failure 200

Known failures are translated through the adapter and API exception-handling mechanisms.

docs.title: 8. Health and readiness
docs.text:
The ingestion service provides independent readiness checks for UC1 and UC3.

UC1 readiness

GET /health/ready

Verifies the UC1 configuration, MongoDB connectivity, and MinIO connectivity.

UC3 readiness

GET /health/ready/coastal-uc3-sentinel2

Verifies:

  • UC3 package availability and bundled resources.
  • UC3 configuration validity.
  • MongoDB connectivity.
  • MinIO connectivity.

Both endpoints return HTTP 200 when ready or 503 when unavailable.

Readiness checks do not execute satellite acquisitions or write data to storage.

UC3 readiness does not prove that CDSE credentials are accepted by the provider or that publication permissions are sufficient.

A readiness failure for one profile does not automatically imply that the other profile is unavailable.

docs.title: 9. Execution and deployment considerations
docs.text:
• Both profiles are executed through the existing FastAPI ingestion service.
  • UC1 and UC3 maintain separate collector implementations and configuration requirements.
  • UC3 is installed as an external Python package and invoked directly through its supported entry point.
  • The UC3 wheel must be supplied during application installation and Docker image construction.
  • UC3 acquisitions remain synchronous from the HTTP caller's perspective, despite executing in a worker thread.
  • Client and reverse-proxy timeouts must accommodate acquisition duration.
  • AOI concurrency guards are process-local rather than distributed.
  • Storage namespaces and permissions must be configured independently for each profile.

docs.text:

The package is not publicly distributed or included in this repository. An authorised package artifact must be obtained from its maintainers or through an approved distribution channel before installation or deployment.

This documentation describes the integration of the external UC3 component into the Data Ingestion Module. It does not claim ownership of the external package or grant redistribution rights. Package usage, modification, and redistribution remain subject to the applicable licence and permissions established by its maintainers.
